slides.title: WRC 2026 Signals Shift Toward Embodied AI Models in Humanoid Robotics
slides.tldr: HUMANOID ROBOTICS SHIFT TO EMBODIED AI
slides.highlight: The shift in humanoid robot competitions from hardware to embodied AI models is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and AI-mediated learning.

slides.title: Prompt Sensitivity of Generative Agents: Evidence from an Epidemic Model
slides.tldr: PROMPT SENSITIVITY IN GENERATIVE AGENT EPIDEMIC MODELS
slides.highlight: This research examines how prompt modifications and persona names affect the behavior of generative agents in an epidemic model, contributing to the development of LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation in MIMIC.

card.one_liner: Generative agents' epidemic behaviors are sensitive to minor prompt variations and context, but not synonymous prompts.
card.key_idea: An epidemic model where agents are prompted daily to isolate or commingle to test sensitivity to prompt modifications and persona names.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a generative agent epidemic model; results show negligible impact from synonymous prompts and persona names, but sensitivity to minor variations.

slides.title: RoboGesture: Real-Time Semantic-aligned Co-Speech Gestures Generation for Humanoid Interaction
slides.tldr: REAL-TIME CO-SPEECH GESTURE GENERATION FOR HUMANOIDS
slides.highlight: This work introduces RoboGesture, a framework for generating synchronized, semantically meaningful gestures in humanoid robots. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: RoboGesture enables humanoid robots to generate real-time, semantically aligned, and collision-free co-speech gestures from audio.
card.key_idea: A framework using a hierarchical semantic-acoustic aligner and a diffusion transformer with anti-inertia CFG masking, supported by a semi-synthetic dataset and MPC-based safety filtering.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on BEAT and SemanticBEAT datasets using FGD, BC, and human studies; outperformed baselines in semantic accuracy and physical consistency.

slides.title: Synthetic Linguistic Agency: How an Embodied Mortal Agent Learns Linguistic Affordances through Consequential Social Experience
slides.tldr: EMBODIED MORTAL AGENT LEARNS LINGUISTIC AGENCY
slides.highlight: This research introduces an Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) that learns linguistic choices based on bodily consequences and social history. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: An Embodied Mortal Agent (EMA) learns to use language strategically to ensure its own survival.
card.key_idea: Mortality-Grounded Linguistic Reinforcement Learning (MGL-RL) couples a body with a viability scale (Reference-RUL), allowing agents to learn linguistic affordances based on partner-specific social consequences.
card.evaluation: Controlled experiments using a 60-encounter social formation process and counterfactual continuations to test the causal roles of embodiment, participation, and precariousness.
card.limitation: The agent's linguistic choices are limited to a fixed action repertoire and rendered via a frozen renderer.

slides.title: AffectSim: A Controllable Interactive 3D Simulation Benchmark for Embodied Affective Perception
slides.tldr: INTERACTIVE 3D BENCHMARK FOR EMBODIED AFFECTIVE PERCEPTION
slides.highlight: AffectSim provides a controllable 3D simulation to study how agent viewpoint and sensing influence emotion perception, supporting the RwB goal of improving human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: AffectSim is a 3D simulation benchmark for studying how embodied agent movement improves affective perception.
card.key_idea: It decouples affective behavior from observation conditions, allowing the same emotion-labeled 3D episodes to be re-observed under varied distances, orientations, and occlusions.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 24 frozen perception models on 27,647 episodes using Macro-F1; a two-stage active-observation baseline improved 21/24 configurations over initial views.
card.limitation: The benchmark currently focuses on the perceptual layer with prescribed affective behaviors, excluding temporally evolving behaviors.

slides.title: Leveraging Turn-taking Dynamics for Intent Recognition in Multi-party Conversations
slides.highlight: This research introduces turn-transition entropy to model interaction patterns in multi-party dialogues, supporting HyECHO's goals in addressee and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: A multi-task learning approach improving multi-party intent recognition by predicting turn-transition entropy as an auxiliary task.
card.key_idea: Introduces a self-supervised regression task to predict turn-transition entropy, quantifying the predictability of speaker transitions to provide contextual cues for intent classification.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on MPGT, MIntRec2.0, and MEETInt datasets using BERT, RoBERTa, and DeBERTa. Results show consistent macro-F1 improvements over single-task and graph-based baselines.
card.limitation: Requires accurate speaker identities for each utterance; performance may degrade if automatic speaker diarization introduces errors.

slides.title: How Much Can AI Understand? Toward AI-Assisted Sensemaking of Collaborative Discussion in Groups with Shared History
slides.highlight: This work proposes a model for AI-assisted sensemaking that captures group norms, participants, and social context in collaborative discussions, aligning with HyECHO's focus on group norms and social perception.

card.one_liner: Proposes an AI model for sensemaking in group discussions that incorporates social context and shared history.
card.key_idea: An AI-assisted model that supports early sensemaking stages (extraction, prioritization, connecting, presentation) by integrating arguments with community norms, participant context, and domain-level discussion topics.
card.evaluation: Based on two studies of experienced Wikipedia editors' cognitive processes and a web-based LLM-assisted prototype; results are not quantitatively detailed.
card.limitation: High system interpretive work risks dehumanizing participants, creating false consensus, and erasing minority opinions due to lack of social intelligibility.

slides.title: Mind the Gap: Theory-of-Mind-Grounded Friction for Epistemic Alignment
slides.highlight: This work introduces a Theory-of-Mind (ToM) framework to detect epistemic misalignment and silent divergence in dialogue. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on addressee/listener modeling and the perception of hybrid team states.

card.one_liner: ToM-grounded friction improves LLM intervention and calibration in collaborative dialogues by modeling second-order belief divergence.
card.key_idea: A four-identifier Theory-of-Mind schema extracts first- and second-order beliefs to compute a friction signal, which conditions Frictive Policy Optimization (FAR/FTR) objectives.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on HCRC MapTask using intervention F1, ECE, and Brier scores; FAR/FTR outperformed DPO in calibration and training stability.
card.limitation: The method relies on an offline GPT-5 extractor for ToM labels, and gains primarily preserve rather than create base-model competence.

slides.title: VocalAffectBench: Evaluating Vocal Emotion Recognition in AI Audio Models
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark to evaluate AI audio models' ability to identify vocal emotions from raw audio, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and engagement.

card.one_liner: VocalAffectBench evaluates AI audio models' ability to recognize expressed vocal emotion from raw audio.
card.key_idea: A test-only benchmark of 280 English clips across seven emotion labels, evaluating models using raw audio without transcripts to isolate vocal affect from lexical sentiment.
card.evaluation: Six baselines (including Gemini 3.5 Flash) were tested; average accuracy was 35.1%, showing significant over-prediction of 'neutral' and fragility in non-neutral classes.
card.limitation: Limited to General American English, uses acted speech rather than spontaneous conversation, and relies on a discrete seven-label taxonomy.

slides.title: Faireez offers housekeeping services to collect data for robot training
slides.highlight: Faireez is collecting data through human housekeeping services to train robots, which is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

slides.title: Counterfactual Explanations and the Scope of Contestability
slides.highlight: This research examines how counterfactual explanations can reinstate human agency in societal domains, supporting MIMIC's focus on the impact analysis of hybrid human-AI societies.

card.one_liner: Analyzes whether counterfactual explanations enable decision-subjects to effectively contest opaque algorithmic decisions.
card.key_idea: Defines contestability as providing sufficient information to revoke decisions and proposes a multi-shot querying approach to improve counterfactual explanations' effectiveness in detecting model errors.
card.limitation: The paper focuses on theoretical accounts and sketches of modifications rather than empirical validation.

slides.authors: Alice C. W. Huang et al.

slides.title: Argument-Aware Semantic Alignment of Normative Texts: A Toulmin-Based Neuro-Symbolic Approach
slides.highlight: This work proposes a neuro-symbolic pipeline using LLMs and Toulmin argument structures to align specialized normative texts, supporting MIMIC's use of neuro-symbolic and LLM-based agent models for societal-scale simulation.

card.one_liner: A neuro-symbolic pipeline using Toulmin argumentation structures improves semantic alignment of cybersecurity normative texts.
card.key_idea: Combines neural embeddings with 12 structured features (claims, grounds, warrants, etc.) derived from LLM-based argument explicitation to capture inferential reasoning in regulatory requirements.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on NERC-CIP and NIST-CSF mappings using Random Forest classifiers; results showed statistically significant F1-score improvements over a neuro-symbolic baseline.
card.limitation: The study uses cybersecurity standards as a controlled testbed and does not claim domain-independent generalization.

slides.title: You Know What I Mean: A Benchmark for Agentic Conversational Reference Grounding
slides.highlight: This work introduces RepoRef to evaluate how agents resolve indirect references by combining conversational context with external workspace evidence, supporting HyECHO's focus on multimodal social perception and listener modeling.

card.one_liner: RepoRef is a new benchmark for resolving indirect conversational references to GitHub artifacts using tools.
card.key_idea: Conversational Reference Grounding (CoRG) requires agents to use GitHub APIs to resolve underspecified references by combining conversational context with external metadata and content.
card.evaluation: Evaluated 9 LLM agents on 400 developer-chat segments. Gemini-3-Flash performed best (67% success), though most agents struggled with commit-level grounding and ambiguous candidates.
card.limitation: Limited to open-source GitHub collaboration (issues, PRs, commits) and uses rewritten messages instead of naturally occurring indirect references.

slides.title: Pairing Google Antigravity with Gemini 3.7 Flash solves notable multi-agent math and engineering problems
slides.highlight: The integration of Google Antigravity and Gemini 3.7 Flash addresses complex multi-agent math and engineering problems, providing insights for MIMIC's focus on agent models.
